findings.what: The batch-level duplicate-key guard in commitSubmissions is no longer falsifiable by any test, because the new CommitDelta constructor refuses the same state with a message that also contains the asserted phrase "same segment". Measured in a copy of the staged tree: replacing the throw with a bare `keys.add(s.segmentKey())` leaves all 211 sequencer tests green, including `twoSubmissionsNamingTheSameSegmentAreRefused`. This is the exact hazard the neighbouring `anEmptyBatchIsRefused` names in capitals ("THE MESSAGE NAMES THE LAYER, and it has to") -- applied to the empty case and not to the duplicate one.
findings.failure_scenario: A later refactor deletes the batch guard as redundant. `commitAll` still refuses a colliding batch, but reports a DELTA-layer message ("a delta names the same segment twice") for a BATCH-layer mistake, so an operator reading the log looks for a corrupt entry rather than for the caller that submitted the same segment key twice. No test fails.

findings.what: The decoder now rejects a byte sequence it previously accepted -- a v1 delta whose segment list names one key twice -- but ADR-0032, which defines this layout and states "Decoding accepts both", does not record the uniqueness constraint. No bytes in any bucket are affected (the only writer never emitted duplicates), and `ChainEntry.decode` wraps the IllegalArgumentException as IOException "corrupt chain entry of kind 0", verified by decoding hand-patched bytes -- so the fail-closed behaviour is right; only the recorded contract is missing.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.8/M4.9, or any later code that merges two windows' segment lists into one entry, is written from the ADR rather than from the record and emits a delta naming one segment key twice. The entry is written once, and from then on every reader's recover() of that epoch fails permanently with "corrupt chain entry" -- there is no skip path -- with nothing in the recorded format saying the writer was at fault.
